clue.text: Has set purpose to explore the Universe!

definitions.text: Has set purpose to explore the Universe!

parts.words: Has set purpose to explore the Universe!
parts.note: the set is a receiving set, a wireless whose purpose is listening to signals from distant stars and galaxies

explanation.surface: Someone has fixed their life's goal on exploring the cosmos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' reads as 'fixed', as in a set purpose, but it is a noun: a receiving set, the dish a scientist listens with.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of astronomer studies the heavens by picking up radio waves with large receiving dishes.

clue.text: Brings up something past description

parts.note: bringing up something from the past is remembering it, while 'past description' tempts a reading of something indescribable

explanation.surface: Someone raises a matter that is beyond words.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a past event back to mind is to remember it, the plain sense of the verb.

clue.text: A tendency to move without purpose

definitions.meaning: to float along aimlessly, as a boat does with the current

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the general trend of something, and aimless floating along.

clue.text: Being ham roll we hear, could be played like this

definitions.text: Being ham roll we hear, could be played like this

parts.words: Being ham roll we hear, could be played like this
parts.note: a ham is a showy actor, and roll said out loud is role, so a hammy part would be performed too theatrically

explanation.surface: A sandwich order seems to be giving stage directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham roll' looks like lunch; 'ham' is a showy actor and 'roll' stands for 'role', which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham actor exaggerates every line, which is performing with too much theatrical emphasis.

clue.text: Vehicles under snow and ice

parts.note: vehicles that run on runners over snowy ground rather than buried beneath it

explanation.surface: Cars are buried under a winter freeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' suggests buried; these vehicles are 'under' snow only in the sense that they are used in those conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleighs on runners are the vehicles used for travelling across snow and ice.

clue.text: Got down snooker ball with new cue-comes to bad end!

parts.note: the red is the commonest ball on a snooker table

indicators.note: something new is made over, so these letters take a fresh order
the end of a word is its last letter, here at the close of 'bad'

explanation.surface: A snooker player pots a ball with a new cue and it all ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CUE as UCE; 'end' takes D, the last letter of 'bad'; 'comes to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something down is to lower or lessen it, so it was made smaller.

clue.text: What's laid in such sheltered places?

definitions.text: What's laid in such sheltered places?

parts.words: What's laid in such sheltered places?
parts.note: eggs are what birds lay, and they do it in sheltered homes built of twigs

explanation.surface: A question about what is put down in hidden spots.
explanation.walkthrough: The thing laid is eggs, which the clue never names.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds build these sheltered homes of twigs and moss specifically to lay eggs in.

clue.text: Relates to man destroying alien scum

indicators.note: destroying smashes the words alien scum apart so their letters can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: A hero defends humanity by wiping out alien invaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying' rearranges the letters of ALIEN SCUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what belongs to men or is manly, so it pertains to the male.

clue.text: Fine cuts of pork!

parts.note: thin slices of cured pig meat, fine meaning thin rather than excellent

explanation.surface: A butcher praises the quality of pork joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' suggests quality; here it means thin, and the pork is the cured kind, bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: These are thin slices of bacon, cured pork cut finely for frying.

clue.text: Their dishes are numbered amongst the finest in Britain, some say

definitions.text: Their dishes are numbered amongst the finest in Britain, some say

parts.words: Their dishes are numbered amongst the finest in Britain, some say
parts.note: takeaway menus from this Eastern cuisine famously list each dish by a number

explanation.surface: Praise for one nation's cooking as among Britain's best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbered amongst' seems to mean 'counted among'; literally the dishes carry numbers on British takeaway menus.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names the people and cuisine of China, whose takeaways number their menu items.

clue.text: Stops being off-side. It's quick way to get a point

annotationWithheld.why: 'Stops being off-side. It's quick way to get a point' (7): OCR text gives no parse for DESISTS; 'off-side' may anagram SIDE but the rest, 'It's quick way to get a point', yields no STS, and no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: Stops being off-side. It's quick way to get a point

clue.text: It means go, begone, in a manner of speaking!

definitions.text: It means go, begone, in a manner of speaking!

parts.words: It means go, begone, in a manner of speaking!
parts.note: go is read as energy or get-up-and-go, so the word describes a state where that drive has gone

explanation.surface: Someone explains a phrase ordering a person away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go, begone' sounds like a dismissal; 'go' is energy, and the word means that energy is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sluggish and listless means having lost all drive, the energy colloquially called go.

clue.text: Relish that may come from bottle neck

definitions.text: Relish that may come from bottle
definitions.meaning: a condiment poured from a bottle, such as ketchup

explanation.surface: A condiment is poured from the narrow top of a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle neck' reads as one thing; 'neck' is the British slang for cheek or nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bottled condiment and cheeky impudence, as in 'none of your lip'.

clue.text: Weird priestess from Kent makes goblins appear

indicators.note: weird suggests the letters of priestess are strangely disordered

parts.note: Kent is a county in South East England, so SE

explanation.surface: An odd priestess from the county of Kent conjures goblins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes SE out of PRIESTESS, leaving PRIESTS, which 'Weird' rearranges; 'makes ... appear' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprites are small mischievous supernatural creatures, close kin to elves and goblins.

clue.text: A drop to drink!

parts.note: a drop is a raindrop as well as a little drink, so this is water fallen from the sky

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a little drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A drop' sounds like a small tot of something; it is a drop of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Water collected from showers is literally drops falling from clouds, and it can be drunk.

clue.text: Women employed to clean up the commonest products of Fleet Street

definitions.meaning: daily helps, cleaners who come in each day

definitions.text: the commonest products of Fleet Street
definitions.meaning: daily newspapers; Fleet Street in London was the home of the British press

explanation.definitionFit: The plural covers both cleaning ladies who come daily and newspapers published every day.

clue.text: Making a part of something else for one consul in trouble

definitions.text: Making a part of something else

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: trouble stirs up the letters so they fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A diplomat finds himself in difficulties abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges I, CONSUL and IN; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Including something makes it part of a larger whole, the act this noun names.

clue.text: He must put up with what he can get

definitions.text: He must put up with what he can get

parts.words: He must put up with what he can get
parts.note: putting up means erecting walls and houses, using whatever materials are available

explanation.surface: A stoic tolerates whatever life hands him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as tolerate; split it as 'put up' (erect) plus 'with' (using).
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman of this kind erects houses and walls from bricks and other materials.

clue.text: Help emergency firefighters by putting them in chains

definitions.text: Help emergency firefighters by putting them in chains

parts.words: Help emergency firefighters by putting them in chains
parts.note: a chain of people passes pails of water hand to hand to douse a blaze

explanation.surface: Sounds like a plan to imprison volunteer firefighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chains' suggests shackles; it is the human chain that passes water along.
explanation.definitionFit: Pails were passed along human chains as the emergency firefighting gear of old.

clue.text: Says what one has in mind for the Eisteddfod, perhaps

definitions.text: Says what one has in mind for the Eisteddfod, perhaps

parts.words: Says what one has in mind for the Eisteddfod, perhaps
parts.note: the Eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of poetry and song, where competitors declaim memorised verse

explanation.surface: Someone shares their plans for a Welsh arts festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What one has in mind' sounds like intentions; it is the poem learnt by heart. The Eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of music and poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak memorised verse aloud to an audience is to declaim it from memory.

clue.text: Henry V ordered lines of such troops pulled back at Agincourt

definitions.text: Henry V ordered lines of such troops pulled back at Agincourt

parts.words: Henry V ordered lines of such troops pulled back at Agincourt
parts.note: the English longbowmen at the 1415 battle drew back their bowstrings, not retreated

explanation.surface: A history lesson in which the king orders a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled back' sounds like a retreat; it is the drawing of bowstrings before loosing arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: These soldiers fought with longbows, the troops that won the battle of Agincourt.

clue.text: Costing sky-high postage rates?

parts.note: sky-high reads as very expensive, but the letters really are flown through the sky

explanation.surface: A complaint about how expensive stamps have become.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky-high' means very dear; literally the post goes by aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Post carried by aeroplane travels through the sky and costs more than surface delivery.

clue.text: Holy man breaking stone over Texan's head

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: breaking shatters the pieces so the letters are put back in another order

explanation.surface: A saint smashes a rock over a Texan's skull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges ST and STONE together; 'over' links; 'head' is headwear, not a skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed cowboy hat, the classic headgear of Texas, is worn on the head.

clue.text: Items in monastery overheads

parts.note: overheads reads as running costs, but these are hoods worn over monks' heads

explanation.surface: An entry in an abbey's account of running costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overheads' means business expenses; read it as things over the head, monks' hoods.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks wear these hoods over their heads as part of the habit.

clue.text: Polish quarter of Richmond?

definitions.meaning: a gloss or shine on a surface
East ... is a district of the London borough of Richmond upon Thames

explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' hides its sense behind a capital letter; it means shine, not from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a glossy shine and also names a district in southwest London.

clue.text: Valuable stone transporter first bought for relative

parts.note: a car transports people

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the next word, bought

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

explanation.surface: A gem dealer's lorry carries a jewel bought for a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes B from 'bought'; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnet cut in a rounded dome shape is a precious gem called by this name.

clue.text: At a loss what to do if insured

definitions.text: At a loss what to do if insured

parts.words: At a loss what to do if insured
parts.note: at a loss reads as puzzled, but here it is after suffering a loss, when a policyholder asks the insurer to pay

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure of their next step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At a loss' means bewildered; here it means having suffered a loss, which an insurance policy covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Insured people who suffer damage demand payment from their insurer, so they put in a request.

clue.text: Ask a lot, as it were

definitions.text: Ask a lot, as it were

parts.words: Ask a lot, as it were
parts.note: asking a lot means pleading earnestly, with a lot hinting at going a treat

explanation.surface: Someone is being too demanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ask a lot' sounds like being demanding; it means to ask earnestly, to plead.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or plead earnestly is to ask very hard, a strong form of requesting.

clue.text: The French man is ordered to get beasts

indicators.note: ordered puts these pieces into a new sequence

parts.note: la is the French for the

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is commanded to fetch some creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like 'commanded'; it rearranges LA, MAN and IS; 'to get' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Beasts are creatures, the general word for members of the animal kingdom.

clue.text: He doesn't say he's a muscular chap

definitions.text: He doesn't say he's a muscular chap

parts.words: He doesn't say he's a muscular chap
parts.note: a tough type who keeps quiet: the brawny, taciturn hero of fiction

explanation.surface: A modest bodybuilder does not boast of his physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doesn't say he's' reads as modesty; it describes a man who doesn't say anything, and is also muscular.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock figure of a tough, taciturn man is brawny and speaks very little.
